Subject: Pricing exhibit: proposed reallocation and grace band language

Hi Naomi / Ben,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — StellarNet is excited about the latency improvements and the SKU-level insights. Our finance team reviewed the draft pricing exhibit and sent back a short set of redlines focused on the commit/order schedule behavior. Two items are blocking our internal approval:

1) Reallocation window: they want the ability to reallocate unused committed units between SKUs (compute vs. embeddings) without inheriting penalties as long as aggregate committed spend is maintained. They propose a single reallocation per 90-day period.

2) Grace band / true-up: they request a +/-15% grace band on monthly usage before true-ups apply for the first two quarters after go-live, then revert to +/-5%. Also want the true-up timeline extended to 75 days to allow cross-team reconciliation.

We've attached their annotated exhibit for reference. Can Redwood provide proposed counter language that preserves revenue protection but makes the ask operationally easy for StellarNet? Also, please confirm whether the reallocation is a billing-only construct or if it will have implications for capacity reservations.

Appreciate quick turnaround — they're hoping to finalize legal by end of week.

Best,
Daria

Naomi — quick read and suggested guardrails below. I'm attaching suggested redline snippets in the doc Naomi referenced (proposed-orderform-redline-v2.docx).

Legal concerns and recommended language:
- Reallocation: allow one billing-only reallocation per 90-day period subject to written notice. Add explicit language: "Reallocation shall not entitle Customer to change reserved capacity allocations for the purposes of Redwood's capacity planning or SLAs; any reallocation is effective for billing only and does not move reserved GPU capacity between workloads."

- Grace band / true-up: accept a temporary +/-12% band for first two full billing cycles (we can compromise from their 15% ask). After the initial 60 days post-go-live, band reduces to +/-5%. True-up will be performed on a quarterly basis with a 60-day reconciliation window following the quarter end. No cumulative carry-forward of credits beyond 12 months.

- Overages and credits: define threshold-based crediting: if monthly usage exceeds committed plus grace band by >25%, an overage rate applies and Customer is eligible for a one-time mitigation credit only if they notify Redwood within 30 days and can show demonstrable cause (force majeure, migration delay).

Revenue recognition note: billing-only reallocations help limit revenue deferral risk since committed dollars remain; however, frequent reallocation promises could complicate forecasting. Keep reallocation capped at once per quarter and require a signed amendment for any change to reserved capacity.

If team agrees, I'll fold this into the doc and Naomi can send to Daria.

-Michael

Daria — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing StellarNet's annotations. After internal review we've put together a short counterproposal that balances your team's operational flexibility with our need to protect committed economics. Summary below and attached PDF with redline.

Counterproposal (high-level):
- Reallocation: one billing-only reallocation per 90-day period (i.e., one reallocation effective for the following invoice cycle). Reallocation does not change reserved GPU capacity or SLA commitments without a signed amendment.
- Grace band: temporary +/-12% band for the first two full billing cycles post go-live (we can take your 15% ask down to 12%). After those two cycles, band reduces to +/-5%.
- True-up cadence and window: quarterly true-up; customers have 60 days after quarter end to reconcile.
- Overages: if usage exceeds committed + grace band by >25% in any month, an overage rate applies; for one-time migration/force majeure events we will consider a mitigation credit (requires notice within 30 days and finance approval).

Why this is fair: the billing-only reallocation gives StellarNet operational flexibility while preserving Redwood's ability to plan capacity and honor SLAs. The temporary grace band reduces friction during ramp. The quarterly true-up keeps billing cycles predictable.

Next steps: if this aligns, we can (a) add the exact redline language into the pricing exhibit and (b) circulate a DocuSign amendment for signature. I'm happy to hop on a quick call with finance/legal to walk through the mechanics.

Attached: counterproposal-20250821.pdf

Regards,
